youtube.title: 🔥 This Repo Turns Code Into Visual Maps You Can Actually Understand
youtube.description: Ever stare at a massive codebase with no clue where to start? Understand Anything (50K+ stars) turns any project into an interactive knowledge graph you can explore like a map. Run /understand and a multi-agent pipeline scans every file, function, class, and dependency — then builds a visual dashboard with guided tours, semantic search, and architectural layers color-coded for you. No more reading code blind. You get plain-English explanations for every component, impact analysis for your diffs, and even business domain views that show how code maps to real processes. Works natively with Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Codex, Gemini CLI, and more — one-line install for most platforms. The graph is just JSON so you can commit it once and your whole team skips the initial scan. Perfect for onboarding, code reviews, or just understanding that legacy monolith everyone's afraid to touch. Try the live demo at understand-anything.com — pan, zoom, search, and click through a real codebase visualization right in your browser. Link in bio.

linkedin.text:
I just joined a new team last month. 200,000 lines of code. No documentation. The senior dev who built it left two weeks before I started.

I spent my first week just trying to figure out which files talk to which. Drew diagrams on whiteboards. Made my own dependency trees in a notebook. It was brutal.

Then I found Understand Anything.

You run /understand in your terminal and it scans your entire codebase with a multi-agent pipeline — extracts every file, function, class, dependency, and relationship. Then it builds an interactive knowledge graph you can explore visually.

Not just a static diagram. An actual dashboard where you click nodes to see code, relationships, and plain-English explanations.

It has 50,000 GitHub stars because it does something rare: it teaches instead of just impressing you.

You get:
• Guided tours ordered by dependency (learn the codebase in the right sequence)
• Semantic search (ask "which parts handle auth?" and get real results)
• Architectural layer views (API, Service, Data, UI — color-coded automatically)
• Diff impact analysis (see what breaks before you commit)
• Business domain maps (how code maps to actual workflows)

The setup? One command. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Codex, Gemini CLI, and more.

The graph is just JSON — commit it once and your whole team skips the pipeline. Perfect for onboarding or code reviews.

I used it to understand our payment flow in 20 minutes. Would've taken me days otherwise.

There's a live demo at understand-anything.com if you want to see it in action before installing.

If you've ever joined a project mid-flight and felt completely lost, this is the tool that fixes it.

Link: github.com/Lum1104/Understand-Anything
